info.title: TMetric REST API
info.description:
This is the latest version of the TMetric API documentation. Though, it does not cover all the functionality. Use the TMetric REST API to create calls to get the data you need to integrate with TMetric.

See API v2 specification [here](https://app.tmetric.com/api-docs/v2)

## Authentication

You must authenticate all requests to the TMetric REST API, which uses bearer authentication.

__Bearer authentication__ (also called __token authentication__) is an [HTTP authentication scheme](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Authentication)
that involves security tokens called bearer tokens. The name “Bearer authentication” can be understood as “give access to the bearer of this token.”
The bearer token is a cryptic string, usually generated by the server in response to a login request.

The client must send this token in the __Authorization__ header when making requests to protected resources:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```
Where `<token>` is your personal access token, generated by TMetric authorization server. You can get a token from your [profile page](https://app.tmetric.com/#/profile) inside the TMetric web app.

### How to get an API token

1. Click your name in the left bottom corner.
2. Select My Profile in the drop-down list.
3. On the My Profile page, click the Get new API token link.
4. Copy the newly created token and use it to make API requests.

__Note:__ An API token will be valid for 1 year. If you generate a new token, the previous one becomes invalid.

## Errors

For API responses, TMetric uses HTTP status codes, which indicate whether a specific HTTP request has been executed successfully or not. Status codes, which start with 2, indicate success. Codes starting with 4 mean client-side errors (e.g., incorrect syntax, authentication has failed, etc.). Codes that begin with 5 indicate server-side errors (occur rarely). 

| Status code   | Meaning       |
| :-------------| :-------------|
| 400 Bad Request | The request could not be understood by the server. Incoming parameters might not be valid. |
| 401 Unauthorized | The supplied credentials, if any, are not sufficient to access the resource. |
| 404 Not found | The requested resource is not found. |
| 403 Forbidden | The user on whose behalf the request is being made is denied access to the resource. |
| 429 Too Many Requests | Too many requests have been made in a short period of time (Throttling). | 
| 500, 502, 503, 504 - Server Errors | Something went wrong on TMetric's end. (These are rare.) |    

## Account ID and User ID

Most of API requests require __{accountId}__ and __{userId}__ parameters.
* __{accountId}__ is an identifier of a [TMetric workspace](https://tmetric.com/help/workspace-management/what-is-workspace)
* __{userId}__ is a TMetric user identifier.

The best way to get current user's ID and the list of available workspaces is to issue an HTTP GET request to the User API endpoint.

### How to get parameter values from UI

If you don't want to send an extra request, you can get __{accountId}__ and __{userId}__ from the application UI.

To get __{accountId}__ value:
1. Open the Time page in the TMetric web app
2. Copy the number from the browser's address line.
   * The only number if the __{accountId}__ parameter value you need.
   
To get __{userId}__ value:
1. Open the [Project Summary](https://tmetric.com/help/reports/projects-summary-report) report in the TMetric web app.
2. Select a user in the dropdown Team filter (don't select the dynamic 'Me' parameter).
3. Apply the filter. You will get the following string in the browser's address line.
```
https://app.tmetric.com/#/reports/2345/projects?range=thismonth&user=7882
```
4. Copy the __user__ parameter value from the address line.

post.description:
An added time entry will overwrite already existing time entries if they overlap.

## To start the timer 
The timer may be started from:
- the present moment in time, by setting `null` both for the start
and the end time of a time entry (see the explanation of null values in the schema description).
- a definite moment in the past, by setting a value for `startTime`.

## To stop the timer 
There are two ways to stop a timer:
- by modifying `endTime` via [PUT /timeentries](#/TimeEntries/put-accounts-accountId-timeentries-timeentryId)
- by adding a break with `endTime` equal to `null` via [POST /timeentries/break](#/TimeEntries/post-accounts-accountId-timeentries-break)

put.description: Updates one or more time entry details (e.g, description, project, tags, start time and end time).

200.description: The time entry was successfully deleted

delete.description: Removes a specific time entry from the workspace.

post.summary: Adds a break to a timeline.
post.description:
Inserts a break into the timeline.

There are two ways to add a break:
- by stopping the timer of an active time entry and starting the timer of the next time entry after a certain time. To stop the timer, add a break where the start time and the end time are equal to `null`, which will mean stopping time tracking from the current point in time.
- by adjusting the time of inactive time entries - changing the end time of the first time entry and the start time of the second one. You can change the `startTime` and the `endTime` via [PUT /timeentries](#/TimeEntries/put-accounts-accountId-timeentries-timeentryId).

On a successful call, the method returns a list of modified time entries for the day where a break was added to.

put.description:
Task attributes can be modified at any time. When changing a task name, assignee, description, or tags, the corresponding changes will be also applied to all the time entries related to the task. A project can be changed only for a task that does not have a worklog.

If a task is external, its project, assignee, due date, estimate, and tags can be changed in TMetric. A task name and description should be changed in the external system where a task was created.

integration.description: An integration, which a created task will be linked to. When read, is not returned, it is used only in case when an external task is created.

client-basic.title: ClientBasic
client-basic.description: Represents a client who can be assigned to a project.

id.description: Represents the unique client identifier.

name.description: The client's name, usually it's a company's name, e.g, "GreenFogDesign Ltd.".

iconUrl.description: The URL of the client's image.

project-status.title: ProjectStatus
project-status.description: A project status. Done projects are displayed in reports, but they aren't available for tracking time. Archived projects are not available in the reports either.

project-basic.title: ProjectBasic
project-basic.description: A project linked to a current entity.

id.description: A project identifier.

iconUrl.description: A full path to a project icon. It can be a svg, png or jpeg image.

tag-basic.title: TagBasic
tag-basic.description: Extra information added to time entries for easy categorization of time.

id.description: A tag identifier.

isWorkType.description: Indicates whether this tag is work type or not

timeentry.description: A span of working time with the name of the task, which a user performed.
timeentry.title: TimeEntry

id.description: A time entry identifier.

startTime.description: The start time of a time entry, null, when tracking, means the current time.

endTime.description: The end time of a time entry, null means that the timer is running, i.e., the current moment of time and the moment in the future, until a timer is not stopped.

note.description: A note can be added to a time entry, even if the task property is not set.

tags.description: Tags associated with the time entry.

isBillable.description: Specifies whether a time span should be considered as billable, works only if a project is set up and it is billable.

isInvoiced.description: It is an indication of whether a time span is included into the invoice, which actually means that the invoice is blocked for futher changes.

timeentry-break.title: TimeEntryBreak
timeentry-break.description: A time span during which a break is taken from work.

startTime.description: The start time of a break being added to a timeline.

endTime.description: The end time of a break being added to a timeline.

recentUsageTime.description: The last time logged by the current user, which relates to this project. If there are no such time entries for the previous two months, then it returns null.

isBillable.description: Determines whether a project is billable or not

recent-timeentry.title: RecentTimeEntry
recent-timeentry.description: Recent entry for time tracking, may or may not be linked to a task

note.description: Additional description, may be specified separately from the task.

isBillable.description: A flag indicating that the time entry will be a billable.

isPinned.description: A checkbox indicating that the time entry will be pinned in the recent list.

isWorkTypeBillable.description: Determines whether a work type is billable or not

user-basic.description: A registered user who can be a member of one or several workspaces.
user-basic.title: UserBasic

iconUrl.description: The URL of the user's image.

id.description: Represents the unique user identifier.

name.description: The user's full name, e.g, "John Doe". The name cannot include numbers or special characters.

color.description: A color for the policy to distinguish it from others.

modified.description: The timestamp when a task was modified. The time is displayed in the user's local timezone.

dueDate.description: Represents the due date of the task.

estimatedMinutes.description: Represents the approximate amount of time (in hours and minutes) to complete a task.

task.description: Represents an external or internal task.

task-update.title: TaskUpdate
task-update.description: Represents a task being partially modified.

task-change.title: TaskChange
task-change.description: A change made to a specific task.

timestamp.description: The ISO datetime of a change in the requestor timezone.

text.example: changed the name to \"New task name\

oldValue.description: The value that has been changed.

newValue.description: The new value that is used instead of the old one.

individual-schedule.title: IndividualSchedule
individual-schedule.description: The object represents the work schedule information of a particular workspace member.

days.description: The days, which fall within a date range (the start date and the end date of an individual schedule) specified for the filter.

date.description: The date in the schedule displayed.

isWorking.description: Indicates whether a day is working or not.

hours.description: The number of working hours on this date.

team-basic.title: TeamBasic
team-basic.description: Represents a team where workspace members can be added to.

id.description: Represents the unique team identifier.

team-filter.description: Lists of teams and workspace members who requested time off.

teams.description: The teams that workspace members are added to.

users.description: Registered users who can be members of one or several workspaces.

time-off-request.description: A request for days off from work created by a workspace member.

client-related-entities.description: Represents summary information of entities, related to a client

date.description: Any date inside the timesheet period whose statuses should be changed.

users.description: User identifiers whose timesheets should be changed.

comment.description: Timesheet status change comment. Required when status is rejected.

timesheets-status-change-result.title: TimesheetsStatusChangeResult
timesheets-status-change-result.description: Result of changing timesheet statuses for multiple users.

updatedUsers.description: User identifiers whose timesheets were changed.

unchangedUsers.description: User identifiers whose timesheets were not changed because their current status is no longer valid for the requested action.

message.description: Human-readable message describing unchanged users, if any.
message.example: The timesheets for John Doe and Jane Smith have already been approved.

timesheet-setting.title: TimesheetSetting
timesheet-setting.description: Settings for timesheet period and reminders.

firstWeekDay.description: First day of the week as a zero-based index (0–6).

reminderTime.description: Time of day to send the reminder.

timesheet-summary.description: A lightweight summary of a user's timesheet for a single timesheet period.

comment.description: Timesheet status change comment. Required when status is Rejected.

approverId.description: The user ID who should approve this timesheet. Can be omitted.
